clue.text: He recorded his impressions of French chatter

parts.note: de is the French word for of
gas is idle talk or chatter

explanation.surface: Someone noted down what they thought of French gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressions' suggests opinions, but it hints at the Impressionist painter Edgar Degas, who recorded what he saw on canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was an Impressionist painter, recording visual impressions in paint and pastel.

clue.text: Plain or upland, OK?

parts.note: a down is a stretch of rolling upland, as in the South Downs of England
right means OK, as in all right

explanation.surface: A question of geography: is it flat ground or hills?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like flat land, set against 'upland'; it is the adjective meaning blunt or utter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain as in plain rude: utter, thoroughgoing, blunt.

clue.text: Scrape together scrag-end with some good meat

parts.note: the end of the word scrag is its last letter
lean is meat without fat, a good kind

explanation.surface: A cook gathers the cheapest neck of mutton with a little good meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrag-end is a cheap cut of neck meat, but here it means the last letter of 'scrag'.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather bit by bit, like collecting leftover grain after harvest.

clue.text: Dinner has to be cooked for council

indicators.note: cooking prepares raw ingredients into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An evening meal must be prepared for a local committee.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the supreme court and ruling assembly of ancient Jerusalem.

clue.text: Bug in trapdoor hard to mend

indicators.note: mending puts something broken back together in a new way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An insect has got into a trapdoor that will be difficult to repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to mend' rearranges TRAPDOOR plus H; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal bug is any creepy-crawly, and insects, spiders and their kin belong to this jointed-legged phylum.

clue.text: Beautiful, like Raphael?

explanation.surface: Is a lovely painting typical of the Renaissance master?
explanation.walkthrough: Raphael suggests the painter, but here he is the archangel.
explanation.definitionFit: Beautiful as an innocent face can be; and Raphael is an archangel, so like him means of heavenly messengers.

clue.text: Bottom was top for this queen

definitions.text: Bottom was top for this queen

parts.words: Bottom was top for this queen
parts.note: Bottom the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream became, under a love spell, the favourite of the fairy queen

explanation.walkthrough: Bottom is the weaver given an ass's head in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream; the fairy queen falls for him.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's play, enchanted into loving the weaver.

clue.text: Puzzle about raised contribution

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a sub is a subscription, a regular contribution

explanation.surface: A conundrum concerning an increased donation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SUB upwards to BUS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture riddle where symbols and letters stand for words.

clue.text: Fellow eating tiny measure of fruit

indicators.note: eating puts the measure inside the fellow, as if swallowed

parts.note: a fellow is a person
1 mm, one millimetre, is a tiny measurement

explanation.surface: A man is consuming a small portion of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The tiny measure is 1 mm, read as I and MM.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange, tomato-like fruit from Asia and America, often called sharon fruit.

clue.text: Avoid the city

explanation.surface: Steer clear of the town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodge City in Kansas was a famous Wild West town.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade or sidestep; and Dodge City is a town in Kansas famous in Wild West lore.

clue.text: Small man having rest between two spells of work

definitions.text: rest between two spells of work

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
a man is a piece in chess, such as a knight

explanation.surface: A short fellow takes a break between two shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece here, as in 'chessmen'.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening between working days is a time for resting before the next day's labour.

clue.text: Produced daughter with nothing on

parts.note: bare is an archaic past tense of bear, meaning gave birth to or produced

explanation.surface: A woman gave birth to a girl while wearing no clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produced' looks like the definition, but it is the old past tense BARE of 'bear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncovered and exposed has no covering left over it.

clue.text: Sinner half-heartedly resolved to finish washing

indicators.note: resolving here means breaking up and reforming, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the heart of the word is its two middle letters, and losing half of them drops one

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer resolved, without much conviction, to complete the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two central Ns of SINNER, leaving SINER; 'resolved' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The last stage of a wash is clean water to carry off the soap.

clue.text: Great victory for novice with toboggan

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate of a novice driver
and means together with
to toboggan is to slide downhill on a sled

explanation.surface: A beginner on a sled wins by a huge margin.
explanation.definitionFit: An election won by an overwhelming majority is described as a sweeping triumph.

clue.text: Information fine, but nothing special

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
an eric was a compensation fine for killing someone in old Irish law

explanation.surface: Data about a penalty turn out to be unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: ERIC is an obscure word for a blood fine in early Irish law; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbranded or general lacks any distinguishing feature, being ordinary.

clue.text: Be rough in maltreatment of one who should be loved

indicators.note: maltreating something knocks it about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning against being harsh in mistreating a loved one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love thy neighbour' is the biblical command behind the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible commands love for the person next door, as in 'love thy neighbour as thyself'.

clue.text: Painting wrongly said to be Cynthia

indicators.note: said signals that the phrase must be spoken to hear the new word

parts.note: painting is art, and wrongly is amiss, giving art amiss

explanation.surface: A portrait has been mistakenly claimed to depict a woman named Cynthia.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, ART AMISS sounds like the goddess's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cynthia is a title of the Greek moon goddess, from Mount Cynthus where she was born.

clue.text: Reluctance of sailor to eat on vessel

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
to dine is to eat
SS is a steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A seaman is unwilling to have his meal aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is only a link. Tardiness here carries its older sense of slowness or reluctance to act, not mere lateness.
explanation.definitionFit: Slowness or hanging back from acting is an old sense of being reluctant.

clue.text: In mad rush, a wife accepts unauthorised advances

indicators.note: in places a and wife within the rearranged word
mad suggests a crazed jumble, so the letters of rush are rearranged

parts.note: a mate is a spouse, here a wife

explanation.surface: In a frantic hurry, a married woman receives improper overtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges the word rush, and 'In' places the rest inside. The definition describes the person: a sportsperson nominally unpaid who takes money on the quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsperson posing as unpaid who secretly takes money, so pocketing improper payments is the mark of one.

clue.text: Rather poor pub inside, the Royal

indicators.note: inside places the pub within the following words

parts.note: an inn is a pub
R is an abbreviation for Royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: A pub housed within a royal establishment is rather shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor in the sense of meagre or sparse; less substantial means slimmer.

clue.text: Burglar finally doing poorly with fence

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word burglar

parts.note: ailing means unwell, doing poorly

explanation.surface: A thief is making a bad job of it with a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' suggests a dealer in stolen goods beside the burglar; it is a barrier of bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of upright bars forms a barrier or enclosure.

clue.text: Swimmer managed without a hip replacement

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around
a replacement hip is a reworked one, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A swimmer coped without having a hip operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' rearranges A and HIP into PIHA, which goes 'without' (outside) RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This toothy South American fish is a flesh-eating river creature.

clue.text: Fee, but no interest in this bond

explanation.surface: A charge is levied, though this savings certificate pays nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are a British government savings scheme paying prizes by draw instead of interest.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurance payment is a charge; and Premium Bonds are British savings certificates that pay prizes rather than interest.

clue.text: Goethe in ecstasy at first about an apostle

parts.note: Johann was the first name of the German writer Goethe

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word ecstasy

explanation.surface: The German poet in rapture at the start, writing about one of the twelve disciples.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannine means relating to Saint John, one of the twelve disciples.

clue.text: Worn by the casual astronomer?

parts.note: casual trousers worn by anyone, punning on the name of the British astronomer Sir James ...

explanation.walkthrough: Sir James Jeans was a noted British astronomer of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim trousers are casual wear, and the plural surname is that of a famous stargazer.

clue.text: Players whose trapeze act is dangerous?

definitions.text: Players whose trapeze act is dangerous?

parts.words: Players whose trapeze act is dangerous?
parts.note: a group of nine musicians, read as two words saying that the circus act has nothing to catch a falling acrobat

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer describes a trapeze act performed without a safety net.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nine musicians performing together is an ensemble of players.

clue.text: The cricket team you'd expect to come first in a rubber?

definitions.text: The cricket team you'd expect to come first in a rubber?

parts.words: The cricket team you'd expect to come first in a rubber?
parts.note: a rubber is a series of matches, but one national side's name comes first in a rubber of the elastic kind

explanation.walkthrough: A rubber is a cricket series; India rubber is natural rubber, so the country's name comes first before 'rubber'.
explanation.definitionFit: The national side of this subcontinental country plays Test cricket, and its name precedes 'rubber' for latex.

clue.text: Impress with sketch

explanation.surface: Make an impression with a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impress' means to force into service, as press gangs did; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To conscript someone into military service; and a rough preliminary version or outline drawing.

clue.text: The navy is after a firm mast

indicators.note: is after places the navy letters following the others

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The navy is chasing a company's ship mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mast' is not a ship's spar but the fallen nuts of forest trees, once fed to pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mast is the collective name for oak and beech nuts on the forest floor, and an oak nut is one of them.

clue.text: Keep travelling and speed past one point

indicators.note: past places the speed letters beyond the others

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tine is a point or prong of a fork or antler
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A traveller presses on, speeding by a landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: To itinerate is to journey from place to place, as a circuit preacher does.

clue.text: Technique for transposing rock layers

indicators.note: transposing swaps the order of rock and layers as they appear in the clue

parts.note: strata are rock layers
a gem is a precious stone or rock

explanation.surface: Geologists have a method for swapping round layers of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transposing' tells you to swap the clue's order, so the layers come before the rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse or cunning scheme is a method for gaining an advantage.

clue.text: Lusty man appearing a day younger

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday, a day
yr is the abbreviation for younger

explanation.surface: A lecherous fellow looks a day younger than he is.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth these woodland creatures were goat-legged and lecherous, so a lecher is named after them.
